reproductionReviewed.summary: The PRIMARY defect FINDING-8 was created for (recordAnalysisFailureLog's own Postgres write throwing uncaught) was genuinely fixed and reverified against real, unmocked Postgres FK violations (P2003) from two independent upstream call sites (constructions 1 and 2). However the fallback's own bare `console.error(...)` call at the former orchestrator.ts:467-470 had no try/catch of its own. Construction 3 in the auditor's test forced console.error itself to throw (simulating a wrapped/instrumented console - Sentry's console integration, a Winston/pino console transport, Next.js edge-runtime console interception - all realistic production conditions) and captured a stack trace showing the exception propagating directly out of runContractAnalysis uncaught, with the top frames being the injected console.error exception, then `Module.runContractAnalysis (orchestrator.ts:467:15)`, then `processTicksAndRejections` - nothing intervened. This recreated the exact log-only/no-visibility failure mode FINDING-8 exists to eliminate, one tier deeper.

fixSummary.designPrinciple: A genuine, NON-RECURSIVE three-tier fallback hierarchy, with no tier ever calling back into a DB-backed logger from within that logger's own failure path.

tiers.mechanism: recordAnalysisFailureLog(...) - a real, durable Postgres write (AnalysisFailureLog row). Already correct (unchanged by this fix): wrapped in its own try/catch, verified against real Prisma driver exceptions.
tiers.onSuccess: failureRecordPersisted = true. This is the ANALYSIS_FAILED_AND_RECORDED case.

tiers.mechanism: On PRIMARY failure: failureRecordPersisted is set to false, and the recording write's own classified error is captured into a NEW local (`failureRecordError`) that is now RETURNED to the caller in the RunContractAnalysisResult object itself - not just embedded in a console line. The caller therefore always has BOTH the original failure (`fatalError`, never masked or replaced) AND the persistence-failure detail (`failureRecordError`) in the structured result, with no further DB write of any kind attempted. This is the ANALYSIS_FAILED_BUT_DURABLE_RECORD_FAILED case.
tiers.newField: failureRecordError: { message: string; errorClass: string } | null

tiers.mechanism: The console.error call is now wrapped in its OWN try/catch, nested inside the SECONDARY catch block, with an otherwise-empty catch body (no retry, no alternate channel, and above all no call back into recordAnalysisFailureLog/Postgres - that would just be 'log the logging failure' recursing into the same failing abstraction this whole branch exists to route around). Whether the console.error succeeds or itself throws, the function always proceeds to its normal `return` statement - it never lets anything propagate uncaught from this catch block.
tiers.newField: failureRecordFallbackLogged: boolean | null - true when the last-resort console trace was emitted successfully, false when even that itself threw (swallowed, recorded honestly), null when not applicable (failureRecordPersisted is true or null).

fixSummary.resultContractInvariant: `outcome` is always "FAILED" for every case in this branch (never anything success-shaped), in every one of the three tiers above, including when both PRIMARY and the TERTIARY console.error fallback fail. `failureRecordPersisted`/`failureRecordError`/`failureRecordFallbackLogged` are the caller-facing signals that let a caller/operator distinguish ANALYSIS_FAILED_AND_RECORDED (failureRecordPersisted: true) from ANALYSIS_FAILED_BUT_DURABLE_RECORD_FAILED (failureRecordPersisted: false), and further distinguish whether even the last-resort trace landed (failureRecordFallbackLogged). None of these fields, nor `outcome`, nor `status`, is ever set in a way that could be read as analysis completion or success for any branch of this catch block.

handTracedConfirmationNoCodePathCanThrow.conclusion: Every statement in the PRE_RUN_IDENTITY catch block either cannot throw for any input, or is directly wrapped in its own try whose catch does nothing but set an already-declared local flag. There is no longer any statement in this fallback chain capable of propagating an exception out of runContractAnalysis. The other five `RunContractAnalysisResult`-constructing return sites in the file (SKIPPED_NO_CONTRACT_DOCUMENTS, SKIPPED_ALREADY_RUNNING, SKIPPED_SUPERSEDED, the PER_INSTRUMENT_ANALYSIS whole-run-failure branch, STARTED_TO_COMPLETION, and the outer INGESTION_OR_STRUCTURAL catch) were updated only to add the two new required fields as `null` - none of those call sites is part of this fallback chain, and none was otherwise touched.

dispositionRationale: The console.error last-resort fallback (the fix's own designated bottom of the fallback hierarchy) is now wrapped in its own try/catch, making it incapable of throwing uncaught regardless of whether the runtime's console has been wrapped/instrumented. Every statement in the PRE_RUN_IDENTITY catch block was hand-traced and confirmed either provably total or contained by its own try/catch. The result contract now exposes failureRecordPersisted (ANALYSIS_FAILED_AND_RECORDED vs ANALYSIS_FAILED_BUT_DURABLE_RECORD_FAILED), failureRecordError (both the original and the persistence failure, returned to the caller, not just logged), and failureRecordFallbackLogged (whether even the tertiary trace landed) - `outcome` remains "FAILED" in every branch, never success-shaped. No tier of the fallback ever calls back into a DB-backed logger from within that logger's own failure path, verified both by code inspection and by an explicit call-count assertion in the extended test. Construction 3 from the independent Part B recertification, which previously falsified the fix's own claimed invariant, now passes against the fixed code.
